overview_markdown:
ZeptoClaw is a personal AI assistant infrastructure written in Rust, shipped as a single ~6MB binary with ~50ms startup and ~6MB RAM usage. It bundles tools, long-term memory, messaging channels, 18 model providers, and sandboxed autonomy, explicitly positioning itself as a synthesis of lessons from OpenClaw (integrations), NanoClaw (container isolation), NemoClaw (policy-gated guardrails), and PicoClaw (edge efficiency) without their respective tradeoffs.

Architecturally, it emphasizes security and correctness at the edges: container isolation, prompt-injection detection, a circuit-breaker provider stack, tool-schema sanitization for strict providers (Anthropic) and local grammar-constrained backends (llama.cpp), and conservative coercion of malformed tool arguments from small local models. Recent work shows deep attention to the local-model deployment story — parsing `reasoning_content` from OpenAI-compatible endpoints so reasoning models like Qwen3 and DeepSeek distills never return silent empty replies, with explicit guards preventing chain-of-thought leakage into tool calls or streams.

Compared to OpenClaw, ZeptoClaw trades ecosystem breadth for footprint and control: no large TypeScript app, no heavy config surface, and a local-first posture with optional cloud providers. The project maintains a large test suite (3,900+ tests claimed) and active dependency security hygiene (prompt Rustls advisory patching), though it recently removed GitHub Actions CI in favor of local validation gates, and third-party ecosystem digests characterize it as lower-velocity than the leading clones.
